investment_thesis:
At 79.01 per share, the market is pricing Coca-Cola for an implied free cash flow CAGR of 11.53% — a rate that is demanding when measured against a base of 5.30 billion in FY FCF, a five-year EPS growth estimate of 7.05%, and FY revenue growth of 1.87%. KO has historically delivered mid-single-digit organic growth supported by concentrate price/mix; doubling that rate on a cash basis requires either sustained 5-7% price/mix combined with EM volume re-acceleration, or a material FX reversal. None of these are visible in the current trajectory, and the base-case FY+2 EPS of 2.81 sits below trailing non-GAAP EPS of 3.04, reflecting margin and FX pressure embedded in our scenario set.

The FY+2 price target range spans 23.62 at the bear low to 55.04 at the bull high, with the base mid at 29.19 — all below the current 79.01 print. Whether the upper end of that range is reachable depends primarily on Driver A (Global Price/Mix and EM Volume Expansion): without 5-7% sustained price/mix flowing through at concentrate's 60%+ gross margin and EM unit case volume holding low-single-digit growth, the bull EPS of 3.48 and the associated 11.0-15.8× P/E band cannot be defended against peers like PEP (15.8× fwd) and KDP (11.9× fwd).

The probability-weighted expected value is 32.70, implying an expected return of -58.61% against the 79.01 spot price, with a prob_loss of 1.00 across the modelled scenario set. This is not a risk/reward profile that supports accumulation at current levels — the bull outcome itself clears only 55.04, well below today's price, which is the structural problem the rest of this report unpacks.
reverse_dcf_commentary: The 11.53% implied FCF CAGR is demanding relative to KO's demonstrated cash generation. FY FCF of 5.30 billion against FY revenue of 47.94 billion (FCF margin 11.05%) and FY operating margin of 31.1% represent a mature, high-quality cash engine — but one growing reported revenue at 1.87% YoY. To justify 11.53% FCF growth, the buyer is implicitly betting that organic revenue accelerates toward 5-7% on sustained price/mix, that FX drag reverses, that operating margin expands toward 33-34% as concentrate mix improves, and that share count continues compressing through buybacks. Each individual bet is plausible; compounding all four simultaneously over a multi-year horizon is the demanding part, and it is what current price requires.

scenario_commentary.bull: The bull scenario carries a joint probability of 31.58% and resolves to a price target of 55.04 on FY+2 EPS of 3.48 at the upper P/E bound of 15.8×. Realising this requires Driver A to fire positively — 5-7% price/mix flowing through with EM unit case volume holding, consistent with event A1's probability of 35% and the consensus FY1 revenue high of 50.53 billion. Supporting this, Driver B's bull event B2 (probability 25%) requires the bottler franchise system to demonstrate further working-capital strength, building on DSO improvement from 27.7 to 23.1 days. Even with both firing, the bull target sits 30% below current price.
scenario_commentary.base: The base case carries the lowest joint probability at 21.05% and resolves to a price target of 29.19 on FY+2 EPS of 2.81 at a mid P/E inside the calibrated 8.2-12.6× band. This reflects organic growth in line with the consensus FY1 revenue mid of 49.09 billion (+2.4% reported), contained FX headwinds removing 0.2-1.0 billion of revenue per event C2, and operating margin holding near the FY 31.1% level. The base EPS of 2.81 is below trailing non-GAAP EPS of 3.04, reflecting the cumulative drag from FX translation on ~65% non-USD revenue.
scenario_commentary.bear: The bear case carries the highest joint probability at 47.37% and resolves to a price target of 23.62 on FY+2 EPS of 2.62 at the lower P/E bound of 9.0×. The structural risk anchor is Driver C (FX Translation and Sugar/Health Regulation Risk): event C1 carries a 45% probability of removing 1.0-2.5 billion of reported revenue versus organic trend, driven by continued USD strength, sugar-tax expansion across UK, Mexico and US states, and GLP-1 demand impact on sparkling volumes. Operating margin compresses toward 28-30% in this outcome, and the multiple compresses with it as KO trades through KDP toward the lower end of staples.
scenario_commentary.A: Global Price/Mix and EM Volume Expansion is the primary organic growth lever: concentrate price increases pass through bottlers at near-100% incremental margin while EM consumers trading up from informal beverages expand the volume base. With FY operating margin at 31.1% and gross margin at 61.6%, every incremental dollar of organic revenue is highly accretive. The most important event is A1 (bull outcome, 35% probability), supported by the consensus FY1 revenue high of 50.53 billion versus the FY baseline of 47.94 billion — implying up to 2.6 billion of upside if price/mix and EM volume both fire. The distribution leans base (50% probability on A2), with bull at 35% and bear at 15%, reflecting a constructive but not aggressive read.
scenario_commentary.B: Bottler Franchise System Recurring Stability anchors the cash flow base through exclusive bottler contracts, century-old brand equity, and global shelf presence that produce annuity-like concentrate orders. FY operating cash flow of 7.41 billion and FCF of 5.30 billion reflect the durability of this system, and event B1 (base, 60% probability) explicitly references these figures plus FY GAAP net income of 13.11 billion as evidence of recurring franchise economics. The distribution leans firmly base at 60%, with bull at 25% (B2, anchored on DSO improvement from 27.7 to 23.1 days) and bear at 15% (B3, citing FCF divergence flagged in data quality warnings).
scenario_commentary.C: FX Translation and Sugar/Health Regulation Risk is the dominant structural headwind. With ~65% of revenue non-USD, a strong dollar compresses reported figures — visible in FY revenue growth of only 1.87% despite mid-single-digit organic trends. Layered on top: accelerating sugar taxes (UK, Mexico, expanding to US states) and GLP-1-driven demand impact on sugary beverages. The most important event is C1 (bear outcome, 45% probability), which models removal of 1.0-2.5 billion of reported revenue versus organic trend. The distribution leans bear at 45%, with base at 40% and bull at only 15% — this driver is the single largest contributor to the elevated bear joint probability of 47.37%.

driver_narratives.A: Global Price/Mix and EM Volume Expansion is the central organic growth mechanism. Concentrate pricing flows through bottlers at near-100% incremental operating margin given FY gross margin of 61.6%, while EM unit case volume growth in India, Latin America, and Africa expands the underlying base. The defining event is A1 (35% probability, bull outcome), evidenced by the consensus FY1 revenue high of 50.53 billion versus FY baseline 47.94 billion, implying up to 2.6 billion of incremental revenue. The probability distribution leans base (A2 at 50%), with meaningful bull weight (35%) and limited bear weight (15%).
driver_narratives.B: Bottler Franchise System Recurring Stability is the durability anchor. Exclusive territory contracts and unmatched global distribution generate recurring concentrate orders that behave as an annuity even through demand cycles, with at-home consumption substituting for away-from-home in downturns. The defining event is B1 (60% probability, base outcome), evidenced by FY OCF of 7.41 billion, FCF of 5.30 billion, and GAAP net income of 13.11 billion — all reflecting steady franchise economics. The probability distribution leans firmly base at 60%, with bull at 25% and bear at 15%.
driver_narratives.C: FX Translation and Sugar/Health Regulation Risk is the dominant structural drag. With ~65% of revenue non-USD, USD strength alone compresses reported revenue — FY growth of 1.87% on baseline 47.94 billion already reflects this — and is compounded by sugar tax expansion and GLP-1 substitution risk. The defining event is C1 (45% probability, bear outcome), modelling removal of 1.0-2.5 billion of reported revenue versus organic trend. The distribution leans bear at 45%, with base at 40% and bull at only 15%, and is the largest single contributor to the 47.37% bear joint probability.

financial_health: KO's balance sheet and cash generation are structurally supportive but do not bridge the gap between current price and modelled value. FY FCF of 5.30 billion translates to an FCF margin of 11.05% on revenue of 47.94 billion, FY operating margin holds at 31.1%, and FY SBC of 0.279 billion (0.58% of revenue) is immaterial to per-share economics. Net debt of 30.83 billion is manageable against the cash engine but is not trivial — and the FCF base of 5.30 billion runs well below the ~8 billion annual dividend cited in corporate DNA, meaning buybacks and incremental leverage are funding part of capital return. The financial profile supports the durability thesis embedded in Driver B but does not support paying an 11.53% implied FCF CAGR.
recommendation_rationale:
The PASS recommendation follows directly from the math. Expected value of 32.70 against current price of 79.01 implies an expected return of -58.61%, with prob_loss at 1.00 across the modelled scenario distribution. Joint probabilities skew bear (47.37%) versus bull (31.58%) and base (21.05%), and even the bull_high target of 55.04 fails to clear the current price.

The calibration log confirms a Step D consensus_divergent flag: bull_high of 55.04 is at or below current price of 79.01 despite a positive consensus median price target of 88.00. This is the central tension — sell-side analysts model continued multiple expansion and FX normalisation that our scenario probabilities do not support, particularly given the 45% weight on Driver C's bear outcome. The bear P/E was also capped at 10.0× to preserve scenario hierarchy, and the base P/E band was ratio-discounted (15.8→12.6 high, 11.0→8.2 low). Even with these calibrations, there is no scenario path in which the modelled distribution justifies entry at 79.01.
conclusion:
KO is a high-quality franchise with durable cash generation, but at 79.01 the market is pricing an 11.53% implied FCF CAGR that the modelled scenario distribution does not support — hence the PASS recommendation, with expected value of 32.70 and a bull_high target of 55.04 that itself sits below current price.

The monitoring framework centres on three near-term catalysts. The Q1 FY2026 print (April 2026) is the key test of EM volume momentum in Asia Pacific and Latin America and the first read on GLP-1 impact on sparkling volumes — directly informing Driver A. The Q2 FY2026 print (July 2026) will show whether FY organic revenue tracks within the 5-6% guidance range and the FX impact on reported EPS versus the 3.49 consensus FY2 mid — the cleanest read on Driver C. The CAGNY conference (February 2026) will refresh the multi-year capital allocation framework, productivity savings targets, and any refranchising announcements affecting the reported revenue base. A combination of accelerating EM volume, sustained 5-7% price/mix, and visible FX reversal would be required to revisit this PASS.
